newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2972 against the U.S. dollar on Monday in Shanghai from 8.2962 last Friday on continued strong demand for the greenback, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2968.

Traders said the yuan has been consolidating gradually since mid-February, a trend which was temporarily halted by the start of foreign banks operating in the local currency business two weeks ago, with the market expecting the banks to buy yuan.
"With the foreign bank factor digested by the market, dollar buying became active again last Friday and pushed down the yuan again today," said one trader.

The yuan opened little changed at an intraday high of 8.2963 and consolidated to move around 8.2970 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2977 late in trading. Trading was dull with most business done at about 8.2970, traders said.
The yuan hit resistance at the 8.2960 level after rises early last week, they said.
One dealer said the dollar's rise on the world market last Friday might also have been a factor, encouraging some foreign banks to buy dollars on the Shanghai market on Monday.
"There are no new factors at present to support a yuan uptrend, so it is likely to continue to consolidate in the short-term," a second dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2970 on Tuesday.
The yuan ended up at 6.6570 from 6.7300 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0719 against the Hong Kong dollar.
